claim: The first walk trained on a captured scene, certified on that scene: go2-scene-c1 (mjlab's rough recipe - the height scan, no camera - on Neverwhere's hurdle course at the scene's own coordinates, 4,096 worlds, 51,600 env-steps/s) reached iteration 1,017 of 1,500 and died with NaN in the actor's observations; its last checkpoint, model_1000, judged on the scene by the verdict door with the scene in its protocol: survived 38/40, tracked 0/40, Clopper-Pearson 95 % [0, 0.088], error ratios 0.79-1.19 - and the training reward said the same, track_linear_velocity 0.67 of 2.0 against the plane run's 1.69. The scene walker learned to stay up on the course and not to go where it is told; every world starts at the course's start facing the first hurdle, commanded up to 1 m/s in any direction. The press on the scene (E3's plumbing: frames from the head camera inside the env, manifests naming the scene, its gap and its floor's basis) therefore kept nothing: 40 attempts, 38 survived, 0 tracked. The NaN's consistent cause: mjlab's terrain-bounds termination judges an origin-centred grid the scene patch is not, and had been dropped, so a world that walked off the heightfield's edge fell forever; the scene's own bounds termination is in. Also found: the Go2's play config runs 1e9-second episodes, so a press rollout ended only at a fall (fifty minutes in one batch) - capped at the training episode now.

caveats: The NaN's cause is consistent with the terminations recorded (no bounds term; worlds walk 10 m in an episode), not reproduced: the bounds termination is in for the next run, and that run will say.
One run, one seed, 1,000 of 1,500 iterations: the scene walker's number is a first, not a bound on what the recipe can do here; the plane's recipe took 1,500 iterations to 38/40.
The press's criterion is the certificate's (survived and tracked); a survived-only batch would be data of a robot standing on a course, and was not pressed.

The certificate's commands are held twists from the course's start, the plane's protocol on the scene's ground; the course protocol (deploy/course.py) judges the exported form in the gate, which the rough actor's height scan cannot reach yet (docs/78 §8.7).
